analysis:
The change in MediaIngestTests.swift is test-only. It adapts six assertions to a new wrapper type returned by decodeImage, decodeImageData and decodeVideo, now accessed via `.source` (head lines 118, 185, 209, 227, 533, 766). No production code is in the supplied evidence.

The existing security-relevant test coverage is unchanged in the visible text:
- SSRF and local-file-read rejection: http(s):// and file:// URIs still expect MediaError.invalidURL.
- Pixel, byte, frame, image-count and video-count caps.
- In-memory video retention with no plaintext temp file (T-050).
- Narrow purge of legacy video temp files.
- Env-override saturation (no trap).

The supplied head text for 9f8fad7f8b38f6a4:4 is cut off at line 672, so the tail of the file (including the line 766 change) was not fully visible. The test edits are mechanical and weaken none of the assertions I could see.

Remaining question for integration: the new wrapper type (it has a `.source` property) is defined in a production file outside this batch. It might carry extra data, such as a pixel count or other lifecycle metadata. Whether it preserves the fail-closed data-URI-only policy and the memory-backed video guarantees cannot be judged from this test diff. A reviewer should confirm that in the MediaIngest production source. No threat-model regressions are identified from the supplied evidence.
